substantive_analysis.title: A Decade of Human Development
substantive_analysis.publication_identity: Journal of Human Development 1(1), 2000, pp. 17–23; DOI 10.1080/14649880050008746
substantive_analysis.supplied_version: Publisher article with cover page; online-publication date on cover is 3 August 2010
substantive_analysis.edition_relation: Article citation matches the syllabus work; cover date is separately recorded and is not a replacement for the 2000 article year.
substantive_analysis.source_bound_claim: Sen presents human development as plural evaluation and treats the weighting of concerns as a matter for explicit social choice and public discussion.

argument_steps.label: Evaluative object
argument_steps.statement: Human development accommodates several forms of deprivation and well-being rather than treating income as a sufficient index.

argument_steps.label: Weighting
argument_steps.statement: Weights require explicit social choice and public discussion; a mechanical metric cannot establish which interests should count.

argument_steps.label: Application boundary
argument_steps.statement: The study can ask which evaluative criteria and positions enter a record. It cannot infer representative preferences or assign welfare weights from their mere inclusion.
argument_steps.locator_or_basis: Study application; no Cerrillos population evidence supplied

substantive_analysis.permitted_use: Ask which concerns are included in evaluation and who has grounds to contest them.
substantive_analysis.prohibited_inference: Do not manufacture a composite sustainability score or treat employment/revenue as a complete welfare measure.
qualifications: Sen warns against overconcentration on an aggregate index; printed p. 22.
The paper supplies neither local preference weights nor a Cerrillos distributional assessment.
substantive_analysis.missing_dependency: Human source-fidelity and assignment-fit review; original Cerrillos instruments for any case-specific claim
substantive_analysis.case_application_status: proposed analytical use; not a case finding
